analysis.key_info: 本题聚焦英语语音学中‘最小对立对’（minimal pairs）的核心概念，考查考生对音系学基本分析单位的辨识能力；题干列举四组仅有一个音位差异且能区别词义的单词对（/s/ vs /z/, /t/ vs /d/, /m/ vs /n/），意图检验考生能否准确识别其作为音位对立证据的功能。
analysis.option_compare: A. 正确。sip/zip、tip/dip、map/nap 每组均仅在单个音位上存在对立（/s/-/z/、/t/-/d/、/m/-/n/），且该差异导致词义改变，完全符合最小对立对的定义（两个单词仅在一个音位上不同，且处于相同位置，具有辨义功能）。B. 错误。diphthongs（双元音）指单一音节内由一个元音向另一个元音滑动构成的复合元音（如 /aɪ/, /eɪ/），而题干所有单词均为单音节但含单元音（如 /ɪ/），无滑动特征，属典型干扰项——混淆‘发音单位’与‘音位对立’维度。C. 错误。allophones（音位变体）是同一音位在不同语音环境中的非辨义实现形式（如 /p/ 在 pin 中送气、spin 中不送气），而题干中 /s/ 和 /z/ 属于不同音位，能区分 sip/zip，故非变体关系；此选项利用考生对‘语音实现’与‘音系功能’的混淆设障。D. 错误。phonemes（音位）是抽象的、具有辨义功能的最小语音单位（如 /s/, /z/ 各自为独立音位），但题干呈现的是成对的单词组合，而非单个音位本身；该选项以‘组成部分’偷换‘关系类型’，误导考生将‘含音位的词对’等同于‘音位’。

analysis.key_info: 本题核心考查英语语音学中语调（intonation）的类型识别，聚焦‘降调（falling tone）’在陈述句、特殊疑问句、选择疑问句等语境下的典型使用规律；意图是检验考生对英语口语中语调功能（如表达确定性、完结性、权威性）的辨析能力，关键词为‘falling tone’‘bold words’及语境化语调判断。
analysis.option_compare: A项中‘specials’位于一般疑问句末尾，该句为Yes/No疑问句，常规使用升调（rising tone），表未确定、期待回应，故不符合降调；B项中‘job’处于惊讶性附加疑问语境（‘he has lost his job?’），省略主句后，末尾词‘job’承载强烈情感与不确定性，通常用升调或升降调，非典型降调；C项中‘tomorrow’出现在选择疑问句（today or tomorrow）的第二个选项末尾，根据英语语调规则，选择疑问句中‘or’前用升调，‘or’后（即最后一个选项）必须用降调以标示选择范围终结与信息确定性，因此‘tomorrow’为标准降调，正确；D项中‘bath’处于并列结构长句末尾，虽为句末，但全句为无标点分隔的列举式陈述，实际朗读中因信息密度过大，常采用‘平调+弱降’或分段降调，且‘bath’前缺乏明确句法边界（缺冠词/停顿），不构成语法-语调单位（tone unit）的典型降调核，干扰项利用‘句末=降调’的常见误解设置陷阱。

analysis.option_compare: A项正确：‘function and theme’即‘功能与话题’，是课标明文规定的语言知识第五、第六组成部分（与phonetics, vocabulary, grammar并列），其中‘function’指语言交际功能（如请求、建议、道歉等），‘theme’即‘话题’（课标中亦称‘topics’或‘themes’），二者共同构成语言运用的情境基础；B项错误：‘culture and society’属于课程内容六要素中的‘文化知识’范畴，是语言学习的拓展维度，非‘语言知识’本体构成，属典型概念层级混淆干扰；C项错误：‘literature and linguistics’未被列为语言知识组成部分，文学赏析属选修或拓展内容，语言学理论属高校专业范畴，严重超出高中课标要求，属超纲干扰；D项错误：‘discourse and genre’虽在课标‘语篇知识’部分出现（如语篇类型、语篇结构），但‘discourse’和‘genre’归属于‘语篇知识’（textual knowledge），与‘语言知识’（linguistic knowledge）分属课程内容不同维度，属跨类别偷换概念干扰。

analysis.key_info: 本题聚焦英语语音学中音节时长与重音的关系，核心考查‘重音对元音时长的调节作用’这一音系学基本原理；题干意图在于检验考生能否区分音长差异的语音动因（重音驱动 vs. 位置/环境干扰），关键词为‘longer’‘both syllables’‘/ēü/’及因果逻辑词‘because’。
analysis.option_compare: A正确：英语中重读音节内的元音具有时长延长、音高升高、音强增强等超音段特征，第一音节/mɒ/（实际为/ˈmɒt.əʊ/，首音节含/ɒ/而非题干所标/ēü/，但命题意在考察重音导致的时长对比）因承载主重音而元音延长，符合音系学重音延长律。B错误：该选项混淆了辅音前缩短（pre-fortis clipping）现象，但此处/ēü/后接/t/属清辅音，若在非重读音节才可能缩短，而题干强调第一音节更长，故非主因；且‘comes before a consonant’描述不准确（两音节均以元音起始）。C错误：单纯‘在第一音节’不构成时长差异的语音学依据，如非重读首音节（如‘photograph’首音节/ˈfəʊ.tə.ɡrɑːf/中/ə/极短），位置本身无历时性强制力，属典型位置归因谬误。D错误：/ēü/在‘motto’中实际出现在第二音节/əʊ/（拼写o-o），其前后为/t/和/ʊ/（或零界），并非严格‘between two consonants’；且元音夹于辅音间（如CVC结构）通常导致缩短（如bit/bɪt/），与题干‘更长’矛盾，属音系环境误判。

analysis.key_info: 本题考查英语教学法中PPP（Presentation-Practice-Production）模式的适用边界，核心在于辨析该结构化语法导向模型与不同语言技能教学目标的适配性；关键词为'Popular as it might be'（强调表面普适性与实际局限性的辩证关系）和'not considered appropriate'（指向教学法选择的学理依据而非经验判断）。
analysis.option_compare: A. phonetics：PPP可有效用于语音教学（如呈现音标/发音规则→模仿练习→自主产出单词/句子），属典型适用场景，排除；B. grammar：PPP起源于结构主义语言学与行为主义学习理论，本质为语法教学范式，是其最经典、最直接的应用领域，排除；C. vocabulary：虽词汇教学常需语境化，但PPP可通过呈现词义/用法→控制性练习（填空、匹配）→半开放产出（造句），被广泛接受为可行路径，非最佳但非不适当，排除；D. reading：阅读是意义建构的交互过程，强调预测、推断、监控、策略运用等高阶认知活动，PPP的线性、教师中心、形式主导特征易导致‘为读而读’，忽视图式激活、背景知识整合与批判性理解，违背阅读教学的本质规律（如Rosenblatt的读者反应理论、Grabe的阅读认知模型），故被二语习得界普遍认为不适宜——此为唯一符合‘not considered appropriate’的选项。
analysis.trace_back: 依据《普通高中英语课程标准（2017年版2020年修订）》‘教学建议’部分明确指出：‘阅读教学应以意义为中心，避免将阅读课上成词汇或语法讲解课’；《英语教学法导论》（王蔷，2020）第三章指出PPP适用于‘显性知识传授类内容’（如语音规则、语法规则、基础词汇搭配），但‘不适用于培养综合性语言运用能力的技能类教学’；教育心理学中奥苏贝尔‘有意义接受学习’理论支持PPP在结构化知识传递中的有效性，而阅读理解则更依赖加涅‘智慧技能’层级中的‘高级规则’与‘问题解决’，需建构主义支架式教学（如Reciprocal Teaching），与PPP机械操练逻辑相悖。
analysis.explanation: 命题规律：教资考试高频考查教学法‘适用性边界’，常以‘not/least/most inappropriate’设问，干扰项多设置为PPP的常规应用领域（如grammar、phonetics）或表面可行领域（vocabulary），正确项必指向其理论短板所在（如reading、listening、writing process、critical thinking等生成性、策略性、交互性技能）；做题技巧：抓住PPP三阶段本质——‘教师呈现规则→学生机械模仿→有限产出’，凡需意义协商、策略调控、真实语境应对的技能均不匹配；记忆要点：‘PPP=3P=Prescriptive, Procedural, Product-oriented’，只适合‘P’开头的规则性内容（Phonetics, Patterns of grammar, Prescribed vocabulary chunks），绝不适合‘R’开头的技能（Reading, Reasoning, Real communication）。

Passage 1
Among the throngs of Americans prowling the malls and trawling e-commerce sites many are looking out for themselves. Retail-research firm NPD Group said thus far about one third of consumers have engaged in what is called self-gifting. That's up from 12 percent in a typical pre-recession year and up from the 19 percent who said they planned to do so last year. The National Retail Federation the dispenser of all holiday-related data said in 2012 nearly 60 percent of shoppers would do so.
The latest step in the evolution of our burgeoning culture of narcissism? Yes. Self-gifting makes psychological and economic sense given what Americans have endured these years.
THE POST-BUST(破产) era has been a long hard heroic slog of balance-sheet improvement.
Americans have labored to save money and hack away at the huge mountain of debt they accumulated during the credit boom. According to the New York Federal Reserve consumers have knocked down their aggregate debt load from $12.67 trillion in the third quarter of 2008 to $11.31 trillion in the third quarter of 2012; credit-card debt is off $192 billion from the peak. Americans have cut their load by spending more carefully and engaging in that most un-American of traits:
self-abnegation.
After living frugally for so much of the year and for so many years who can blame a parent at an Apple Store for buying herself a new iPad? Indeed self-gifting may actually be a function of the new abstemiousness. Let's say you've been holding off on replacing your old television. Why not buy it around November or December when insane promotions and free shipping are available?
Besides it's not like self-gifters are solely interested in self-pleasure. An NRF survey said that the typical self-gifter would spend about $140 on himself this year. For comparison's sake the survey said the typical shopper would spent about $750 in all.
After a long period of economic madness(remember the housing bubble and the dotcom mess)self-gifting is a sign of much-needed economic rationality. Shopping for others involves a certain amount of wrong guesswork with negative financial consequence. This year for example CEB TowerGroup claims that Americans will load $110 billion onto gift cards and give them as presents.
But the market-research firm says that about 1.6 percent of that total about $1.7 billion will go unused. Meanwhile a large percentage of gifts wind up getting returned. Adults surveyed by BIG insight in November 2012 found that 35 percent of people reported returning at least some of their gifts. Returns induce guilt and raise the specter of uncomfortable conversations about what happened to that giant striped sweater. But more significant returns are bad for the environment.
They lead to more trips to the mall higher shipping costs and the unnecessary use of packaging materials.
These days the rise of e-commerce means shopping is now antiseptic: sit and click. With the charm gone we have to come up with other ways to make the experience pleasurable.
As the song goes "Have yourself a merry little Christmas".
{TS} What have the retail research and surveys revealed about self-gifting?

It is an age-old practice for most Americans.
It has been on the rise since the recent recession began.
It has reflected the American tradition of self-abnegation.

Passage 2
Among China's greatest art treasures are the Buddhist caves near Dunhuang. Their ancient frescoes and sculptures have survived wars environmental damage antiquities hunters and the chaotic Cultural Revolution.
Today domestic tourism is the biggest threat: the UNESCO World Heritage site has an optimal capacity of 3000 per day but peak times can see twice that many visitors.
The Mogao Grottoes are especially vulnerable to mass tourism. Their ecosystems are fragile. A buildup of humidity and carbon dioxide from visitors' breath can lead to flaking and discoloration of wall paintings.
To preserve the caves the Dunhuang Academy is pioneering a project to digitize the site.
Recently the Arthur M. Sackler Gallery in Washington D.C. offered a tantalizing glimpse at the undertaking. Donning 3-D glasses visitors were transported into a breathtaking "virtual" Dunhuang grotto known as Cave 220. The 3-D interactive experience is flooded with vivid color close-up details moving images of flying bodhisattvas even sound "Dunhuang ranks as the single most important repository of early Chinese art. Here the great cultures of the World--Greek and RomanPersian and Middle Eastern Indian and Chinese--constantly interacted for over a millenniumsaid Mimi Gates, who formed the Dunhuang Foundation. High-resolution digitization will provide a lasting record of this artistic treasure for all mankind and can make it accessible beyond China."
A dozen years ago the Dunhuang Academy began cooperating with foregoing institutions to conserve the treasures. Among the projects one used a camera to create a digital archive of the caves. The results will be used in the academy which planned ＄40 million state-of-the-art visitor center which will present virtual tour of the caves to save the real site wear and tear. The scope of the project is daunting. It requires 20 minutes or so to record a 9-square-meter fresco and there are 492 caves with murals inside. But the Sackler exhibit proved how enthralling the single virtual cave CaB be.
Real caves provide no lightbulbs. Once they reach critical levels of moisture and temperaturethey are shut to the public. Only a few dozen caves are accessible at any given time. But the Sackler's virtual tour was different. One of the most popular features was the "magnifying glass"which can zoom in on say a zither depicted in a mural. The instrument appears to pop out of the wall enlarge and then rotate in space. Visitors can also "flip" back and forth between the intricate Tang-dynasty mural and a later cruder Sung-dynasty fresco.
To help Cave 220's Tang dancer paintings magically come to life two Chinese performers were flown to the Applied Laboratory for Interactive Visualization and Embodiment (ALIVE) in a Hong Kong university. For three days the dancers were filmed performing intricate steps fluid movements and careful manipulation of long sinuous ribbons. They appeared in the Sackler tourdancing as if in midair clad in brightly colored Tang costume. ALIVE's project manager said while he's become intimately familiar with the images Cave 220 he hasn't been there yet. "I can't wait to visit the real thing."
{TS}Which of the following factors mentioned in the article may cause a severe damage to the Buddhist caves today?
